children: WINNIPEG, Manitoba--Canola futures on the Intercontinental Exchange were under pressure for the second straight session Thursday morning, dragged down by vegetable oils.

Chicago soyoil lost more than one U.S. cent per pound, while European rapeseed and Malaysian palm oil were also lower. However, crude oil improved slightly amid ongoing uncertainty between the U.S. and Iran.

Rain is expected for most of Alberta Thursday under cooler temperatures, with the Grande Prairie area seeing between 50 and 100 millimetres. Saskatchewan and southern Manitoba will receive rain with normal temperatures.
The Canadian dollar was up three-tenths of a U.S. cent compared with Wednesday's close. The Bank of Canada announced on Wednesday it was keeping its key interest rate at 2.25%.
Nearly 19,300 contracts were traded. Prices in Canadian dollars per metric ton as of 8:54 CDT:
